title: Slab-and-Span Memory Profile Generator for Long-Context LLMs (Llama/Mistral/Qwen)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build an automated profile generator that produces 'slab-and-span' memory allocations and per-layer memory curves for model variants (Llama 2-family, Mistral variants, Qwen) under long-context configurations (32k, 65k, and custom).

Background: Current memory planners use coarse per-model heuristics or static profiles that do not capture allocator fragmentation, per-layer slab needs, or the interaction between continuous batching and KV cache sharding. As customers push longer contexts and mixed workloads, we see edge cases where OOMs occur at specific sequence lengths or where throughput is suboptimal due to overconservative reservations.

Scope: Produce an offline tool that: (1) runs representative instrumentation traces across model variants and sequence-length buckets to estimate slab sizes, span coalescing patterns, and peak ephemeral working set per-layer; (2) synthesizes a compact profile (CSV/JSON) with: slab regions, span thresholds, layer-by-layer max_kv_bytes, quantization-aware adjustments, and recommended soft-eviction thresholds for continuous batching; (3) integrates generated profiles into the runtime memory planner so the serving runtime can select model-and-length-specific allocations at startup or dynamically reconfigure when token-length distribution shifts.

Key design decisions and proposed approach:
- Instrumentation harness: use a deterministic token replay harness that exercises attention and kv-cache growth for common prompt families (chat, document, code). Collect fine-grained memory samples at layer granularity and allocation-site histograms.
- Slab-and-span model: represent GPU heap as a set of typed slabs (e.g., KV-cache, activations, temporary buffers) with span buckets inside each slab. Span coalescing heuristics will be inferred from allocation histogram to estimate fragmentation risk.
- Bucketed profiles: generate profiles for sequence-length buckets (0-2048, 2049-8192, 8193-32768, 32769-65536) and for mixed-batch shapes to support continuous batching decisions.
- Quant-aware corrections: incorporate measured reductions from int8/4-bit quantized kernels into estimated slab sizes (we'll run small-scale quantized runs to produce correction factors).
- KV-shard interplay: output per-shard kv sizing suggestions for sharded runtime modes, including max shard size and per-request reserve to avoid cross-shard OOMs under bursty batching.
- Runtime integration: profile files must be small (<128KB) and include a version tag. Runtime will pick profile by (model_hash, quant_mode, bucket_id) and can fall back to a conservative default.

Metrics and acceptance criteria:
- Accuracy: generated profile slab peak estimates must be within 8% of observed 99th percentile GPU memory usage across a holdout workload for each bucket and model variant.
- Latency/regressions: applying profile should not degrade p99 latency more than 5% for typical traffic; throughput should improve for workloads previously limited by over-reservation.
- Stability: runtime should not log new OOMs attributable to profile selection in 72h of load testing (simulated traffic).
- File size & performance: profile generation for a single model/variant should complete in under 3h on a single A100-80GB instance in our CI cluster.

Planned experiments:
1) Baseline collection for Llama-70B, Mistral-22B, Qwen-14B across 4 bucket sizes using the instrumentation harness (week 1).
2) Run quant-aware correction experiments with int8 kernels (week 1-2).
3) Validate slab-span predictions against long continuous-batching runs with KV sharding enabled (week 2).
4) Generate profile artifacts and run rollout with canary traffic on dedicated machines (week 3).

Rollout plan:
- Phase A: Offline generator + CI job that commits profiles to artifacts storage and verifies acceptance criteria.
- Phase B: Runtime consumes profiles behind a feature flag; canary 5% of production traffic for 72h.
- Phase C: If stable, enable by default for selected models and expose opt-out config for customers with custom memory constraints.

Acceptance docs and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/SLABSPANS-123 (design + diagrams)
- Generator prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/mem-profiles/pull/47
- CI job: runtime-1.22/profiles-generation (pipeline)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Instrumentation overhead could perturb allocator behavior. Mitigation: use minimal sampling + replay on un-instrumented runs for validation.
- Risk: Fragmentation patterns vary across GPUs (A100 vs H100). Mitigation: include GPU-type correction factors and prioritize H100 in production testing.
- Risk: Profiles become stale as kernels change. Mitigation: add profile regression tests in release pipeline and re-generate profiles on kernel or model recompiles.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket. Initial hypothesis: fragmentation and slab mismatch are causing tail OOMs when we run long-context workloads with continuous batching. Proposing a slab/spans-based profile generator to produce per-model, per-bucket allocations.

2026-02-23 - Diego Martinez: Spiked on Llama-70B with the replay harness. Early findings: a large fraction of ephemeral allocations are coming from residual fused-kernel temporaries rather than KV-cache for short answers; for long context KV dominates after ~8k tokens. Saved raw allocation traces at gs://redwood-internal/profiles/ENG-31472/raw/.

2026-02-26 - Diego Martinez: Pushed prototype harness in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/mem-profiles/pull/40. Instrumentation adds 4% runtime overhead during collection. We should validate that correction is reliable by running non-instrumented replay and comparing peaks.

2026-03-02 - Jeff Huang (review): Reviewed the slab+span model. Suggested we add span consolidation thresholds that map to CUDA allocator behaviors and capture per-kernel transient spikes. Also flagged need to run tests on H100 (internal infra ticket INFRA-980).
